fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so the property can be identified quickly from the road.
• Mark the access drive entrance with reflective posts on both sides to keep it visible at night or in low-visibility conditions.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles so responders can reach both structures without delay.
• Trim vegetation along the access drive so it does not narrow the travel lane or reduce overhead clearance for larger response vehicles.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the detached structure so responders can approach and work around it without obstruction.
• Clear a path along at least one side of the main residence connecting the front to the rear so responders are not stopped at the building perimeter.
• Keep the patio area clear of stored items that could block movement around the rear of the residence.
• Mark or post the location of any rear gate so responders arriving at the front can quickly identify a route to the back of the property.
• Keep any gate on the access drive unlocked or secured with a knox-style lock so responders are not delayed at the entry point.
• Designate a flat, open area near the access drive entrance for staging equipment, keeping it free of parked vehicles and stored items.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches that hang directly over or touch the house roofline and any attached structures.
• Thin trees within the cluster closest to the house to create gaps between individual tree canopies.
• Remove shrubs growing immediately against the exterior walls of the house.
• Keep grass mowed short in areas between scattered trees and the house.
• Clear any dead grass, leaves, or plant debris that has collected against the foundation or along the base of exterior walls.
• Separate shrubs from the base of any fences or outbuildings connected to the main structure.
• Trim lower branches off large trees near the house up to a height that keeps them well clear of shrubs and grass below.
• Keep the areas under tree clusters free of fallen branches and accumulated leaf litter.
• Maintain short grass across open areas between scattered trees to reduce the amount of dry material that can carry fire toward the house.
